320: I have met every type of person alive. In the end, they all want a second bag of pretzels.
321: I walk more in one flight than most people walk in a week, all in a very narrow hallway.
322: I've calmed nervous flyers, crying babies, and grown adults who wanted the shade just so.
323: People treat the cart like a surprise. It comes every flight. It has never once not come.
324: I demonstrate the seatbelt with great care. Everyone watches the one thing they already know.
325: I've handed out thousands of cups of water. People take one sip, then hand it right back to me.
326: I ask 'chicken or pasta' so often I dream it. The dream has no correct answer either.
327: I remember faces for exactly one flight. Then they land and become someone else's problem, kindly.
328: My smile is professional and my feet are honest. Only one of them survives the whole trip.
329: People ask where we are. I tell them the sky. They wanted more detail. So did I, once.
330: First-time flyers grip the armrest. Thousandth-time flyers grip it too, only with more practiced calm.
331: I point at the exits with two flat hands. It is the calmest I look all day, and it is a lie.
332: Someone always presses the button the moment I sit down. I no longer fight it. The button wins.
333: I collect the little cups afterward. So many little cups. A quiet parade of little cups.
334: I've comforted people afraid of turbulence by pretending I have never once thought about it.
335: The job is mostly kindness and balance, delivered sideways, while carrying something hot.
336: I know every word on the safety card. I have watched exactly no one else read a single one.
337: People board tired and leave tired. In between, they mostly want a blanket and a snack.
338: I have said 'welcome aboard' more times than my own name. I answer to both now.
339: My cart is small, the aisle is smaller, and somehow everyone's elbow still finds it.
340: I send bags all over the world. Some of them see more of it than their owners do.
341: A suitcase left this morning. It will arrive somewhere. We are both hopeful about where.
342: I have lifted every kind of bag. The heavy ones are always labeled 'fragile, this way up.'
343: People trust me with everything they packed. I trust the belt, and the belt is doing its best.
344: Some bags travel farther than I ever will. I wave them off like a proud, tired luggage parent.
345: I match every bag to a tag. Now and then a bag decides it would rather go on holiday alone.
346: I learn a lot about people from their suitcases. Mostly that they packed too many shoes.
347: A bag went one way and its owner the other. They will be reunited. Probably. Eventually.
348: I have seen a suitcase held together with one hopeful strap and a great deal of optimism.
349: My job is to keep bags in order. The bags have their own ideas about order.
350: Every day I move a small city's worth of belongings, and none of them thank me.
351: People ask if their bag will make it. I say yes with the calm of a man who is only mostly sure.
352: I've handled a suitcase heavier than me. It won. I filed the paperwork from the floor.
353: A bag once traveled to three places before its owner. It came back with no stories to share.
354: I read the tags all day. It is like reading everyone's travel plans without any of the fun.
355: The belt goes round and round. Sometimes a lonely bag rides it for hours, seeing the sights.
356: I return lost bags to grateful people. The bags say nothing. The bags never say anything.
357: Some luggage arrives before its owner and just waits there, quietly pleased with itself.
358: I have grown fond of one green suitcase. It travels the world constantly. I have never once left this room.
359: My whole day is other people's things going elsewhere. I stay by the belt, and the belt stays with me.
